commits.primary_mechanism_v1: If computeIfAbsent races with itself for the same cache name (two threads both miss the key before either inserts), UserManagedCacheBuilder.build(true) will be called twice for the same name; the second built cache is discarded but was already started (build(true) starts it), causing a started cache to be orphaned and never closed
commits.primary_mechanism_v2: [logic-error] Observable: ClassCastException at the call site when a second caller requests the same cache name with different K/V types. Root change: +userCaches.computeIfAbsent(name, key -> ...newUserManagedCacheBuilder(keyType, valueType).build(true)) stores caches keyed by name alone, ignoring types. Mechanism: cacheManager.getCache() validates types and returns null on mismatch; the new userCaches map returns the existing UserManagedCache regardless of the requested keyType/valueType—a caller requesting the same name with different types receives a cache built for the original types, and the unchecked cast (Cache<K,V>) succeeds via erasure but subsequent put()/get() calls throw ClassCastException inside Ehcache's type-checking layer.

commits.primary_mechanism_v1: If SpringCamelContext receives a ContextRefreshedEvent from a parent ApplicationContext before the child context is fully initialized then CamelContext starts with an incomplete bean registry at CamelAutoConfiguration.java:camelContext bean
commits.primary_mechanism_v2: [lifecycle-ordering] Observable: CamelContext starts with zero routes registered, causing all message routing to silently fail or throw 'No consumers available' at runtime. Root change: -        SpringCamelContext.setNoStart(true); in CamelAutoConfiguration. Mechanism: Previously `setNoStart(true)` unconditionally deferred startup until RoutesCollector explicitly triggered it; the new scheme relies on SpringCamelContext receiving `ContextRefreshedEvent` strictly after RoutesCollector (LOWEST_PRECEDENCE-1 < LOWEST_PRECEDENCE). Any third-party `ApplicationListener<ContextRefreshedEvent>` that also implements `Ordered` with a value between those two constants, or any listener without `Ordered` that Spring inserts ahead of SpringCamelContext, can cause Camel to start before routes are added.

commits.primary_mechanism_v1: If a caller supplies a MESSAGE_HISTORY_HEADER_FORMAT string with fewer than 4 format specifiers (e.g. omits one %s), then String.format will throw MissingFormatArgumentException at MessageHelper.java:printMessageHistory header line, crashing the entire dump and potentially swallowing the real exception being logged
commits.primary_mechanism_v2: [input-validation] Observable: Exchange processing aborts with an uncaught java.util.IllegalFormatException (MissingFormatArgumentException or IllegalFormatConversionException) during message-history dump, corrupting or silencing error output. Root change: +goMessageHistoryHeaeder == null ? MESSAGE_HISTORY_HEADER : goMessageHistoryHeaeder. Mechanism: MessageHelper.java/messageHistoryStacks — the user-supplied string from getGlobalOption is passed verbatim to String.format() with four fixed positional arguments (RouteId, ProcessorId, Processor, Elapsed); a custom format with a wrong specifier count (e.g. only two %s) or a type mismatch (e.g. %d for a String) throws an unchecked IllegalFormatException that propagates out of the dump method; because this method is typically called inside exception/error handlers, a secondary exception here can swallow or permanently lose the original failure context.

commits.primary_mechanism_v2: [null-reference] Observable: NullPointerException when the route stops or the scheduler shuts down after startup took the 'trigger already exists' path. Root change: the entire else-branch omits any assignment to the instance field `trigger`. Mechanism: the if-branch always assigns `trigger = TriggerBuilder.newTrigger()...build()`; the else-branch skips it entirely, leaving the field null; any subsequent code that reads `trigger` (e.g. doStop unscheduling) dereferences null at QuartzScheduledPollConsumerScheduler:doStop.

commits.primary_mechanism_v1: If metadata.enums() contains values with leading/trailing whitespace (e.g. 'FOO, BAR') then enums.add(val) inserts ' BAR' with a leading space, producing corrupt enum lists in the generated component docs and potentially causing validation failures at runtime.
commits.primary_mechanism_v2: [input-validation] Observable: Generated catalog JSON lists enum values with leading/trailing whitespace (e.g., ' VALUE2' instead of 'VALUE2'), causing broken UI dropdowns or catalog validation failures for any EIP or data-format option annotated with @Metadata(enums = "A, B, C"). Root change: +                String[] values = metadata.enums().split(",");. Mechanism: CoreEipAnnotationProcessor.java attribute-processing branch — split(",") produces tokens that include surrounding whitespace characters; no trim() or normalizing split pattern is applied before enums.add(val), so the raw token (including spaces) is written into the TreeSet and ultimately emitted into the generated JSON catalog. The identical unsanitized split is duplicated in the element-processing branch.

commits.primary_mechanism_v1: If any existing caller passes a Class<?> object to getPrimitiveType (which previously accepted Class<?>) the code will now fail to compile or, if an overload exists elsewhere, silently call the wrong method, causing all types to be classified as null/unknown
commits.primary_mechanism_v2: [input-validation] Observable: Any component option whose JSON schema default value is a negative integer (e.g. maxMessagesPerTask, ttl, transactionBatchCount) will be parsed and stored as its absolute value — e.g. '-1' becomes '1' — in every tool, catalog lookup, and generated documentation. Root change: +(\d+) appended as group 4 to PATTERN. Mechanism: In parseJsonSchema at JsonSchemaHelper.java, the matcher calls find() on the raw JSON token; when the token is '-1', the '-' character is not consumed by any group so the engine advances one character and group 4 (\d+) matches only '1', silently corrupting the stored default. The .adoc changes in the diff (maxMessagesPerTask, ttl, transactionBatchCount all flipping from -1 to 1) are the observable symptom of this exact corruption.
